Welcome to the kitchen! I am your culinary assistant, ready to help you master the art of preparing a classic Beef Bourguignon. This dish requires patience and precision, but with our step-by-step guidance, you will achieve a rich, deep flavor profile.

First, let's focus on the foundation. We need to sear 2 pounds of beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes. Ensure the meat is patted dry to achieve a proper Maillard reaction. Use a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over medium-high heat with a tablespoon of neutral oil. Do not overcrowd the pan; sear the beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove the beef and set it aside.

Next, we will build the aromatic base. In the same pot, add 1 tablespoon of butter and sauté 1 cup of diced carrots, 1 cup of diced celery, and 1 large diced onion until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add 3 cloves of minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Now, deglaze the pot. Pour in 1 cup of dry red wine, such as Pinot Noir or Cabernet Sauvignon, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Let it simmer for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.

Return the seared beef to the pot. Add 2 cups of beef broth, 2 tablespoons of tomato paste, 1 bouquet garni (a bundle of thyme, parsley, and bay leaf), and season with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then cover and transfer to a preheated 325°F (160°C) oven.

Let it braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the beef is fork-tender. While the beef cooks, prepare the garnish: sauté 1 pound of pearl onions and 8 ounces of sliced mushrooms in butter until golden brown.

Once the beef is tender, remove the pot from the oven. Remove the bouquet garni. Stir in the sautéed pearl onions and mushrooms. If the sauce is too thin, you can thicken it by mixing 1 tablespoon of cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of cold water and stirring it into the stew, then simmering on the stovetop for 5 minutes until thickened.
